classification.difficultyReason: Infer the common square side and sector radius from equal-length marks, then add two square areas and a 135-degree sector area.

content.prompt: The diagram to the right shows two squares and a sector. Find the area of this figure, leaving your answer in terms of $\pi$.

spec.description: Two equal squares and an unshaded 135-degree sector share a centre vertex. The upright square extends right and down; the other square extends left with diagonally oriented sides. All eight square sides carry matching single ticks. Right-angle marks occur at the leftmost vertex and the upright square's bottom-left vertex. Ordinary source blue outlines and the centre marker are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: Each square has side 4 cm. The sector has radius 4 cm and spans counterclockwise from the rightward radius to the upper-left radius through 135 degrees. The three interiors do not overlap.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no area calculations or answers appear.

answer.short:
$(32+6\pi)\text{ cm}^2$.

Add the areas of the two squares and the sector.
answer.worked:
The matching ticks show that both squares have side $4\text{ cm}$ and the sector has radius $4\text{ cm}$. The sector occupies $\frac{135}{360}=\frac38$ of a full circle.
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{squares}}&=2\times4^2\\A_{\text{squares}}&=32\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{135}{360}\times\pi\times4^2\\A_{\text{sector}}&=6\pi\text{ cm}^2\\A_{\text{figure}}&=(32+6\pi)\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$$
